conviction_note: PL's reaction distribution is violently bimodal (median absolute move 25.98% over 7 prints vs 18.23% implied), so even a real directional tilt collapses to a small signed expectation: I read roughly 55-58% odds the soft-forward-metric branch (second consecutive sequential RPO decline, EBITDA guided below last year's actual) beats the beat-and-raise branch, and 0.42x(+22) - 0.58x(-18) is about -1 to -4 points; I set -3.0 because the negatives I found are forward-looking metrics rather than revenue misses, and 63% has already come out of the price.

findings.finding: Planet's remaining performance obligations FELL sequentially last quarter - $852.4M at 2026-01-31 to $816.0M at 2026-04-30, a $36.4M decline against $94.2M of revenue recognised, i.e. RPO book-to-bill of roughly 0.6 - and the May-July quarter now being reported contains no announced nine-figure booking at all, only two seven-figure deals (Scottish Government, 30 Jul; a European defence customer PR'd 9:01am today), so a second consecutive sequential RPO decline is likely while the headline still shows a large YoY gain.
findings.why_not_priced: Planet reports RPO only as a YoY percentage ('+81% YoY to $816 million') and the sequential figure has to be differenced by hand across two releases. On the 2026-06-04 Q1 FY27 call not one of the covering analysts raised the sequential decline - questions went to pipeline, competition and AI - and the name carries only three estimates. Every wire account of the -25.98% reaction on 05-Jun attributed it to the $1.5B ATM filed that morning, not to bookings; if bookings momentum were priced, the June sell-off would have been framed as a backlog-quality de-rating and the sell-side preview today would be about RPO rather than about the $102-107M revenue guide and EBITDA breakeven.
findings.independence: Two independent legs point the same way: (a) the Q1 FY27 earnings call transcript confirms no analyst asked about the sequential RPO move - https://www.theglobeandmail.com/investing/markets/markets-news/motley/2317887/planet-labs-pl-q1-2027-earnings-transcript/ (2026-06-04); (b) Planet's own announced-deal flow for the quarter, which it PRs down to seven figures, contained nothing large - https://satnews.com/2026/08/03/planet-labs-secures-seven-figure-agricultural-data-contract-with-scottish-government/ (2026-08-03) and https://www.stocktitan.net/news/PL/planet-signs-7-figure-agreement-with-european-defense-and-z4dgwwz0x9dy.html (2026-09-03 09:01 ET). Note this finding and finding 3 both ultimately rest on Planet's own quarterly releases, so treat them as one source cluster with two distinct metrics.

findings.finding: Planet's own Q3 FY26 release states the NRO renewed its baseline EOCL contract for PlanetScope broad-area monitoring for $13.2M 'through June 2026' - so Planet's anchor US intelligence contract expired inside the quarter just reported, and no renewal has been announced anywhere in the June-September 2026 window even though Planet press-released two seven-figure European deals in that same window.
findings.source_date: 2025-12-10 (date confirmed from the URL path segment 20251210)
findings.why_not_priced: The expiry date is buried in a highlights bullet of a nine-month-old press release, not in any calendar or estimate revision. Planet discloses US-government renewals inside earnings releases rather than as standalone PRs, so there is no wire item for the market to react to and no analyst note keyed to a June-2026 expiry. If this were priced there would be a visible bear note on US-government revenue continuity and the 25-delta skew would exist and be positive; the baseline reports no skew at all and a call-heavy 0.59 put/call open interest ratio.
findings.independence: Independent context from a different outlet: the administration's proposal to cut NRO's Electro-Optical Commercial Layer funding from ~$300M/yr to ~$200M, with Planet and BlackSky bearing the brunt if Maxar is fully funded - https://spacenews.com/satellite-firms-brace-for-potential-imagery-budget-cuts-in-2026/ . That article is from 2025 and is itself priced; it is cited only as corroboration that the renewal was not a formality, not as new news.

findings.finding: FY27 adjusted EBITDA is guided to $0-10M against FY26 actual adjusted EBITDA of $15.5M - profitability guided DOWN while revenue is guided up ~41% - and the EBITDA range has stayed $0-10M through two upward revisions to both revenue ($415-440M to $425-441M) and gross margin (50-52% to 52-54%), which arithmetically requires roughly 30% opex growth; Planet's job board currently carries 114 open requisitions, overwhelmingly quota-bearing sales, pre-sales and customer-success roles in Berlin/Netherlands/UK.
findings.why_not_priced: The wire framing for this print is 'path to adjusted EBITDA breakeven', which is inverted - Planet was already at $15.5M of adjusted EBITDA in FY26 and is guiding to at best $10M in FY27. If the market held the correct framing, a Q2 adjusted EBITDA of $0-5M would read as a year-on-year step down rather than as a breakeven milestone, previews would lead on the opex ramp, and the stock would not be quoted on a revenue-growth multiple. Nobody reconciles a raised gross-margin guide against an unchanged EBITDA guide, because the two live in different bullets of the same release.
findings.independence: The 114 open roles and their department mix are from a completely different source - https://job-boards.greenhouse.io/planetlabs (retrieved 2026-09-03) - and corroborate the implied opex ramp; FY26 actual adjusted EBITDA of $15.5M is from https://www.tradingview.com/news/tradingview:709103f111d6b:0-planet-labs-delivers-record-fy26-revenue-307-7m-backlog-900m-fy26-adj-ebitda-15-5m/ (2026-03-19). Shares the company-release source cluster with finding 1 but uses a different metric.

findings.finding: The one thing that has historically broken Planet's satellite-services revenue recognition - launch and delivery slippage - did not happen this quarter: three additional Pelicans launched 2026-05-03 and Pelican-11, the Gen-2 technology demonstrator, launched 2026-07-07 on Transporter-17, both inside the 1 May - 31 July window that the $102-107M guide depends on.
findings.source_date: 2026-05-03 (date confirmed from the URL path segment 20260503)
findings.why_not_priced: The entire 20-day (-16.1%) and 5-day (-9.9%) run-in is explained by two things that have nothing to do with Planet's delivery record - the 2026-06-05 $1.5B ATM filing and rotation out of space names into SpaceX, which listed on Nasdaq 2026-06-11. Nothing in the tape or the coverage distinguishes Planet's own execution, and no wire story has connected the May and July Pelican launches to the satellite-services revenue that the Q2 guide requires. If the market were pricing on-time delivery, the drawdown would have decoupled from the sector rather than tracking it day for day.
findings.independence: Two separate corroborations: the Pelican-11 launch is its own release - https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260706488031/en/Planet-Launches-Pelican-11-Satellite (2026-07-06/07) - and BlackSky, the nearest listed comparable, printed +50% YoY revenue, its first positive quarterly adjusted EBITDA of $4.7M, international subscriptions +150% YoY and a reaffirmed FY26 guide on 2026-08-06, i.e. after Planet last spoke: https://blacksky.com/press-releases/blacksky-reports-second-quarter-2026-results/

searched_and_found_nothing: Intra-quarter ATM usage, the single biggest overhang: I built a share-count series off the Form 144 filings (322,655,231 at 2026-04-15, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1494211/000195004726003520/primary_doc.xml ; 332,908,730 at both 2026-07-10 and 2026-07-23, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1572854/000195004726007280/primary_doc.xml ). The identical July figure on two different filers' forms means the brokers are quoting the stale 10-Q cover number, so it reveals nothing about ATM draws. The +10.25M step is fully explained by the 9,090,913 public warrants exercised at $11.50 that completed 2026-04-27 plus routine RSU vesting. No 8-K or prospectus supplement after the 2026-06-05 Equity Distribution Agreement.

Hedge-driven or bearish positioning build from the range-forward component of the ATM: short interest is 28.5M shares / 8.7% of float and DOWN 12.1% period-on-period (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/PL/short-interest), the opposite of what forward-purchaser borrow would look like.

Executive departure or quiet governance 8-K in the run-in: the only post-print filings are the 2026-06-04 10-K/A, the 2026-06-05 ATM 8-K/S-3, and the routine 2026-07-09 annual-meeting 8-K (directors, KPMG, pay plan all approved).
A launch failure, satellite anomaly or constellation deorbit event inside the quarter - none found.

Federal procurement obligation data (USAspending / FPDS / SAM.gov) for Planet Labs Federal Inc. inside the quarter - the APIs are POST-only and not reachable with the tools available here, so I could not independently confirm or refute the NRO baseline renewal.

Planet's own newsroom, developer changelog, status page and docs for a pricing change, product deprecation or API break - nothing in the window; the pulse blog in August 2026 is almost entirely SEO/education content.
Customer-complaint clusters on forums or a review-volume shift - nothing.

Two promising leads that turned out to be misdated: the EUR240M German government satellite-services deal is 2025-07-01 (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20250701149801/en/), and the NRO commercial-imagery budget-cut story is June 2025. Both fully priced.
SKY Perfect JSAT's own disclosure of JSAT Beyond Innovation capex pace as a cross-check on the $230M Pelican build revenue - no 2026 interim disclosure found.
baseline_tension: The baseline offers no directional statement to argue with - the 25-delta skew is null and the 0.59 put/call open interest is actually call-heavy - so my mild negative tilt cuts against the option book's positioning but agrees with the -9.9% five-day and -16.1% twenty-day run-in, which is exactly why the signed number is only -3.0 against an 18.23% implied move: much of the bearish case is plausibly already in a stock that is 62.9% off its high, and the more striking baseline fact is that 18.23% implied sits well below the 25.98% median of the last seven prints, i.e. the market is underpricing the tail rather than mispricing the direction.
